Web design Des Moines businesses need often comes down to one word: trust. Greater Des Moines is home to more than 80 insurance company headquarters, according to the Greater Des Moines Partnership, and that industry shapes the small business world around it. Around it work independent agents, financial advisors, claims adjusters, body shops, restoration contractors and the lawyers and accountants who serve all of them. Their customers are careful people making careful decisions, and they read a website closely before they call.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, building sites by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas. You see a free demo first. The price is printed and paid once: $497, $997 or $1,997.

What an independent agent's website has to prove

When someone in Urbandale is shopping for home and auto coverage, they are comparing you with a dozen other agents and with a carrier's own website. The agent who wins the call is often the one whose site answers the quiet questions: Are you licensed in Iowa? Which companies can you quote? Will a real person help me when I file a claim? How far are you from me?

Those answers belong on the first screen and on a page of their own, written by someone who asked you, not pulled from a carrier's brochure.

Checklist for a Des Moines insurance or advisory site

Use it to judge your current site, ours or anyone's.

  • Your Iowa license or registration stated accurately, with the lines of coverage you are authorized to write.
  • The carriers you are appointed with, only if each one allows it, and no logos you do not have permission to use.
  • What happens after a loss: who answers, when, and the number to call, separate from the sales line.
  • The towns you serve by name, from Des Moines out to Ankeny, Waukee, Johnston or Indianola, with an office address that matches your Google Business Profile.
  • A short, honest about page with your real name and background, because people buy coverage from a person.
  • A quote request form that emails you every lead, with only the questions you truly need answered up front.

The same list works with small changes for financial planners, tax preparers, adjusters and the auto body and restoration shops that see a lot of insurance work.

Eleven days in August

The other big date on the Des Moines calendar is the Iowa State Fair. The 2025 fair ran August 7 to 17 and drew 1,160,121 people, the third-highest attendance in its history, even through heat and rain; the record of 1,182,682 was set the year before. The Common Sense Institute estimated fairgoers spent about $85 million at the fair.

For a food vendor, a craft maker or a small brand selling at the fair, those eleven days can be a big share of the year. Plenty of fairgoers will meet you there, love what you sell and then search your name a week later from home. If all they find is an old social media post, the sale ends there. A simple site with what you make, where to buy it the rest of the year, catering or wholesale details and a way to get in touch keeps that customer.

Des Moines website design that names the right part of town

People in the metro describe where they are by neighborhood or suburb, and your pages should use the same names. The Partnership describes the Historic East Village as trendy and artsy, packed with independent shops. The Avenues of Ingersoll and Grand are known for local boutiques, home decor stores and a growing restaurant and bar scene. Historic Valley Junction in West Des Moines has more than 120 shops, galleries and eateries. Beaverdale, one of the largest of the city's 51 recognized neighborhood associations, is known for its brick houses and a small business strip on Beaver Avenue.

The suburbs are growing fast. Iowa's Legislative Services Agency ranked Waukee and Ankeny first and second among Iowa cities for population gain in its 2025 report, and Ankeny had about 77,800 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. The whole Des Moines and West Des Moines metro reached 758,539 people. Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence, so a contractor based in Ankeny who wants work in Waukee needs a page that is honestly about working in Waukee. No one can promise you a ranking, and we never will. We can make your site clearly about your work in the towns you name.

Common questions

How much do web designers charge in Des Moines?

Rates vary a lot. Some freelancers bill by the hour, many agencies quote a project price after a meeting, and website builders charge a monthly fee that never stops. Ours are fixed and printed: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for keyword research and a page for every town and service worth targeting, all one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Is Des Moines website design different for an insurance agency?

The building is the same; the content is not. An agency site has to answer trust questions quickly: your license, the lines you write, the carriers you are appointed with, who to call after a loss and the towns you serve. Many carriers have rules about how agents use their names and logos, so check with them before anything carrier-branded goes live.

Do you offer Des Moines web development, or just design?

Both, for what a small business usually needs: pages designed, written and built, a contact form that emails every lead to you, and the titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema set up for search. Custom software, such as a quoting engine tied to carrier systems or a client portal, is a development project for a different kind of firm, and we will say so before you buy.

Should my business have a page about the Iowa State Fair?

If you sell there, yes. A short page that says where to find you on the grounds, what you will have and your fair hours gives fairgoers something to find when they search your name in August. Keep it up year round and update it each summer, so it builds history instead of starting over.

Do I have to meet a web designer in Des Moines in person?

Not with us. Dominion Web Design Pro has no Des Moines office. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and works by phone, email and shared links. You see a free demo of your site before paying anything.
